mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for four consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% month-over-month indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST < -1% month-over-month) signals a divergence between income growth and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to uncertainty in demand allocation.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% AND HOUST < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months, combined with a decline in average hourly earnings growth (implied by UNRATE and PAYEMS dynamics), signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer purchasing power and corporate pricing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months AND PAYEMS growth < 0.2% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter for two consecutive quarters signals a late-cycle demand expansion, which elevates earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > +1% q/q above trend for 2 consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.
